maya: quick update — I'm seeing reproducible memory growth during replay/warmup when kv pages are stored in INT8. Started when we switched the longctx tests to 64k tokens and enabled int8 packing for kv. dump attached in thread (perfheap_180250).

oliver: can you summarize the pattern? is it steady growth or spikes?

maya: mostly steady growth over the first ~40k tokens, then plateaus but at ~20% higher resident than bf16 baseline. CPU profiles show a lot of small memcpy + page faults. suspect fragmentation + page-size mismatch with quantized slots.

ryan: hmm. are we evicting/paging at slot granularity or page granularity? we recently changed eviction to 8MB pages to reduce TLB churn.

maya: eviction is at page granularity (8MB), but the quantized slots for int8 are denser so more slots per page. fragmentation seems to increase because some pages get partially filled but never reused due to slot alignment rounding.

oliver: any evidence that KV reuse is failing? like warmup misses causing re-reads from main memory?

maya: yes — replay warmup hits are low (30-40%) for the first 10k tokens, compared to 80% with bf16. Looks like prefix matching logic falls back when we have partial page hits.

maya: snippet from profiler:```
hot path: kv_lookup -> check_page_bitmap -> if partial_hit: fallback_to_scan -> alloc_temp_buffer -> memcpy -> schedule_eviction
```

sasha: partial_hit -> fallback_to_scan is expensive. could we try allowing partial-page reuse by returning an iterator instead of full-slot materialization? that would avoid memcpy for contiguous ranges.

ryan: safe idea but tricky with quantization since alignment & dequant cost matters. If we keep page pinned during iterator consumption we might avoid extra page faults. pin_count++ on reuse.

maya: I tried a prototype: pin on first partial hit, stream out only requested KV ranges, and do on-the-fly dequant. Memory growth dropped ~12%, and resident matched bf16 after plateau. perf hit ~3ms extra per partial hit due to dequant math, but overall tail latency improved since we avoided paging.

oliver: can you share config you used?

maya: config pasted:```
kv.eviction.policy=LRU
kv.page.size=8MB
kv.pin_on_partial_hit=true
kv.partial_streaming=true
quant.profile=int8_dynamic
kv.slot.align=64
```

sasha: nice. any accuracy impact from int8 dynamic when you stream partial pages?

maya: ran our accuracy harness on the same prompts — tiny regression (~0.6 perplexity increase on a narrow set) but within expected for int8. No extra degradation from partial streaming vs full materialization.

ryan: ok that's promising. we should run longer-run soak (24h) and also check compaction behavior — maybe compaction frequency needs bump when using int8 to avoid accumulation of partially used pages.

maya: agreed. next steps: 1) run 24h warmup soak with pinning enabled 2) telemetry to count partial_hits, full_hits, pinned_pages, page_faults 3) evaluate increasing compaction cadence from 1h->15m on int8 tenants

oliver: add a quick flag so we can A/B pin_on_partial_hit per tenant. Also gate on model sequence length > 32k so we don't regress small-ctx inflight.

dev-bot: deployment scheduled: eng-runtime/kv-pinning-proto -> canary on ded-01 at 1802510000 (ping @oncall)

sasha: small note — if compaction runs too often it may increase CPU and cause more tail. let's monitor CPU% during soak.

maya: yep will capture. I'll paste the soak dashboard and the telemetry schema once the run starts. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
